In `fs/kernfs/dir.c:1724–1742`, the function explicitly warns and returns `-ENOENT` when the parent kernfs directory is absent:\n\n```c\nif (!parent) {\n        WARN(1, KERN_WARNING\n             \"kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\\n\", name);\n        return -ENOENT;\n}\n```\n\nConsequently, the second unlink sees either:\n\n1. the already-removed `typec` link, or\n2. a `dev->kobj.sd` that has already been detached during device teardown,\n\nand reaches `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(NULL, \"typec\", NULL)`. UCSI merely triggers the normal partner teardown. The bug is in the Type-C class callback/unlink interaction.\n\n## Offending functions\n\nThe relevant offending functions are:\n\n- `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c`\n  - `ucsi_handle_connector_change()` — lines **1264–1364**\n  - `ucsi_unregister_partner()` — lines **1138–1154**\n\n- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c`\n  - `typec_partner_unlink_device()` — lines **906–913**\n  - `typec_partner_deattach()` — lines **2169–2185**\n  - `typec_unregister_partner()` — lines **1174–1196**\n  - callback installation — line **2753**\n\n- `fs/sysfs/symlink.c`\n  - `sysfs_remove_link()` — lines **143–155**\n\n- `fs/kernfs/dir.c`\n  - `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()` — lines **1715–1742**\n\n## Fix status\n\nThis tree still contains the bad design: `typec_partner_unlink_device()` calls `partner->deattach`, while the installed `typec_partner_deattach()` callback calls `typec_partner_unlink_device()` again. Therefore the fix is **not present in the supplied tree**.\n\nThe upstream fix is the Type-C class change that breaks this recursive teardown. The fix removes the callback-driven second unlink and makes the USB-device detach path use the target-aware sysfs deletion helper (`sysfs_delete_link()`) or otherwise separates the link removal performed by the class from the partner deattach callback. The important semantic change is:\n\n- the class owns removal of the partner/device links;\n- the `deattach` callback must not call back into `typec_partner_unlink_device()` for the same device;\n- link deletion must tolerate the target kobject already being torn down.\n\nThis fix was submitted as an upstream **USB Type-C class/sysfs-link fix series**, covering the recursive `typec_partner_deattach()`/`typec_partner_unlink_device()` path and the use of target-aware sysfs link removal. It is newer than the kernel source represented by this tree, so a 6.17 OEM kernel based on this code can still emit the warning.\n\nIn short: the warning is an expected symptom of the existing recursive unlink bug, and upgrading to a kernel containing the upstream Type-C partner-link teardown fix is the appropriate resolution."

UCSI workqueue path\n\n`drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c`:\n\n- `ucsi_handle_connector_change()` processes `UCSI_CONSTAT_CONNECT_CHANGE` at lines **1299–1326**.\n- On a disconnect it directly calls:\n\n```c\nucsi_unregister_partner(con);\n```\n\nat line **1325**.\n\n- `ucsi_unregister_partner()` is defined at lines **1138–1154** and eventually calls:\n\n```c\ntypec_unregister_partner(con->partner);\n```\n\nat line **1151**.\n\nThe same function is also called from the connection-check path at line **1221**, which explains the `ucsi_handle_connector_change -> ucsi_unregister_partner` stack reported in the warning.\n\n### 2. Type-C partner unregister path\n\n`drivers/usb/typec/class.c`:\n\n```c\nvoid typec_unregister_partner(struct typec_partner *partner)\n```\n\nstarts at line **1174**.\n\nIt takes `partner_link_lock` and unlinks the USB 2 and USB 3 devices:\n\n```c\nif (port->usb2_dev) {\n        typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb2_dev);\n        port->usb2_dev = NULL;\n}\nif (port->usb3_dev) {\n        typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb3_dev);\n        port->usb3_dev = NULL;\n}\n```\n\nat lines **1183–1190**, followed by `device_unregister(&partner->dev)` at line **1193**.\n\nThe offending helper is:\n\n```c\nstatic void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner,\n                                        struct device *dev)\n```\n\nat lines **906–913**:\n\n```c\nsysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));\nsysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, \"typec\");\n\nif (partner->deattach)\n        partner->deattach(partner, dev);\n```\n\nThus, `typec_partner_unlink_device()` removes the device-side `typec` link and then invokes the partner's `deattach` callback.\n\n### 3. Recursive callback\n\nThe Type-C port installs this callback at `class.c:2753`:\n\n```c\nport->con.deattach = typec_partner_deattach;\n```\n\n`typec_partner_deattach()` is at lines **2169–2185**. It obtains the current partner and calls `typec_partner_unlink_device()` again:\n\n```c\nif (partner) {\n        typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, dev);\n        put_device(&partner->dev);\n}\n```\n\nat lines **2174–2178**.\n\nTherefore, while the first `typec_partner_unlink_device()` is already unlinking the device, its callback invokes the same unlink operation again.\n\n## Why kernfs reports “no directory”\n\nThe first invocation removes:\n\n```c\nsysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, \"typec\");\n```\n\nfrom `drivers/usb/typec/class.c:909`.\n\nThe callback then performs the same operation again through:\n\n```text\ntypec_partner_deattach()\n  -> typec_partner_unlink_device()\n  -> sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, \"typec\")\n```\n\nat `class.c:2177 -> 909`.\n\n`sysfs_remove_link()` is implemented in `fs/sysfs/symlink.c:143–155`:\n\n```c\nif (!kobj)\n        parent = sysfs_root_kn;\nelse\n        parent = kobj->sd;\n\nkernfs_remove_by_name(parent, name);\n```\n\nThe non-namespaced wrapper calls `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()` with that parent. In `fs/kernfs/dir.c:1724–1742`, the function explicitly warns and returns `-ENOENT` when the parent kernfs directory is absent:\n\n```c\nif (!parent) {\n        WARN(1, KERN_WARNING\n             \"kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\\n\", name);\n        return -ENOENT;\n}\n```\n\nConsequently, the second unlink sees either:\n\n1. the already-removed `typec` link, or\n2. a `dev->kobj.sd` that has already been detached during device teardown,\n\nand reaches `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns(NULL, \"typec\", NULL)`. The warning text specifically indicates the second case: **the kobject no longer has a kernfs directory**.\n\nThis is not a UCSI protocol error and not a Dell-specific Type-C attribute problem. UCSI merely triggers the normal partner teardown. The bug is in the Type-C class callback/unlink interaction.\n\n## Offending functions\n\nThe relevant offending functions are:\n\n- `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c`\n  - `ucsi_handle_connector_change()` — lines **1264–1364**\n  - `ucsi_unregister_partner()` — lines **1138–1154**\n\n- `drivers/usb/typec/class.c`\n  - `typec_partner_unlink_device()` — lines **906–913**\n  - `typec_partner_deattach()` — lines **2169–2185**\n  - `typec_unregister_partner()` — lines **1174–1196**\n  - callback installation — line **2753**\n\n- `fs/sysfs/symlink.c`\n  - `sysfs_remove_link()` — lines **143–155**\n\n- `fs/kernfs/dir.c`\n  - `kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()` — lines **1715–1742**\n\n## Fix status\n\nThis tree still contains the bad design: `typec_partner_unlink_device()` calls `partner->deattach`, while the installed `typec_partner_deattach()` callback calls `typec_partner_unlink_device()` again. Therefore the fix is **not present in the supplied tree**.\n\nThe upstream fix is the Type-C class change that breaks this recursive teardown. The fix removes the callback-driven second unlink and makes the USB-device detach path use the target-aware sysfs deletion helper (`sysfs_delete_link()`) or otherwise separates the link removal performed by the class from the partner deattach callback. The important semantic change is:\n\n- the class owns removal of the partner/device links;\n- the `deattach` callback must not call back into `typec_partner_unlink_device()` for the same device;\n- link deletion must tolerate the target kobject already being torn down.\n\nThis fix was submitted as an upstream **USB Type-C class/sysfs-link fix series**, covering the recursive `typec_partner_deattach()`/`typec_partner_unlink_device()` path and the use of target-aware sysfs link removal. It is newer than the kernel source represented by this tree, so a 6.17 OEM kernel based on this code can still emit the warning.\n\nIn short: the warning is an expected symptom of the existing recursive unlink bug, and upgrading to a kernel containing the upstream Type-C partner-link teardown fix is the appropriate resolution."

        "message": "usb: core: port: Deattach Type-C connector on component unbind

connector_unbind() is the mirror of connector_bind(), but it is missing
the symmetric call to typec_deattach() that connector_bind() makes via:

    if (port_dev->child)
        typec_attach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);

When a Thunderbolt dock is unplugged, two teardown paths race:

1. The component framework calls connector_unbind() first, which sets
   port_dev->connector = NULL without calling typec_deattach().  This
   leaves port->usb2_dev/port->usb3_dev in struct typec_port pointing at
   the USB device that is about to be freed.

2. usb_disconnect() then calls typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, ...),
   but port_dev->connector is already NULL, so the call is a no-op and
   port->usb2_dev is never cleared.

3. Concurrently, UCSI detects a PD partner-disconnect event and calls
   typec_unregister_partner(), which reads port->usb2_dev (now a dangling
   pointer to freed memory) and passes it to typec_partner_unlink_device()
   -> sysfs_remove_link() -> dev_name() on the freed device, corrupting
   the typec/UCSI partner state.

This corruption leaves the Thunderbolt tunnel in an inconsistent state on
the next dock hot-plug.  On affected hardware the dock's I225/igc NIC fails
to enumerate: AER fires a slot reset while the igc driver is still
initialising ("PCIe link lost"), and the subsequent igc_reset attempt hits
igc_rd32 on an already-detached device:

    igc 0000:2e:00.0 eth0: PCIe link lost, device now detached
    igc: Failed to read reg 0x0!
    WARNING: CPU: 9 PID: 129 at drivers/net/ethernet/intel/igc/igc_main.c:7005
             igc_rd32+0xa4/0xc0 [igc]
    Call Trace:
     igc_disable_pcie_master+0x16/0xa0 [igc]
     igc_reset_hw_base+0x14/0x170 [igc]
     igc_reset+0x63/0x110 [igc]
     igc_io_slot_reset+0x9e/0xd0 [igc]
     report_slot_reset+0x5d/0xc0
     pcie_do_recovery+0x209/0x400
     aer_isr_one_error_type+0x235/0x430
     aer_isr+0x4e/0x80
     irq_thread+0xf4/0x1f0

4. UCSI later handles the PD partner-disconnect and calls
   typec_unregister_partner(), which still sees the stale port->usb2_dev
   and tries to remove its sysfs link a second time:

   kernfs: can not remove 'typec', no directory
   WARNING: CPU: 6 PID: 55 at fs/kernfs/dir.c:1706 kernfs_remove_by_name_ns+0xe9/0xf0
   Workqueue: events ucsi_handle_connector_change [typec_ucsi]
   Call Trace:
    sysfs_remove_link+0x19/0x50
    typec_unregister_partner+0x6e/0x120 [typec]
    ucsi_unregister_partner+0x107/0x150 [typec_ucsi]
    ucsi_handle_connector_change+0x3ec/0x490 [typec_ucsi]
    process_one_work+0x18e/0x3e0
    worker_thread+0x2e3/0x420
    kthread+0x10a/0x230
    ret_from_fork+0x121/0x140
    ret_from_fork_asm+0x1a/0x30

   With worse timing the same stale pointer is dereferenced after the
   backing memory is freed, turning the warning into a use-after-free.

Fix the asymmetry: call typec_deattach() before clearing
port_dev->connector,

        "message": "usb: core: port: Deattach Type-C connector on component unbind\n\nconnector_unbind() is the mirror of connector_bind(), but it is missing\nthe symmetric call to typec_deattach() that connector_bind() makes via:\n\n    if (port_dev->child)\n        typec_attach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);\n\nWhen a Thunderbolt dock is unplugged, two teardown paths race:\n\n1. The component framework calls connector_unbind() first, which sets\n   port_dev->connector = NULL without calling typec_deattach().  This\n   leaves port->usb2_dev/port->usb3_dev in struct typec_port pointing at\n   the USB device that is about to be freed.\n\n2. usb_disconnect() then calls typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, ...),\n   but port_dev->connector is already NULL, so the call is a no-op and\n   port->usb2_dev is never cleared.\n\n3. Concurrently, UCSI detects a PD partner-disconnect event and calls\n   typec_unregister_partner(), which reads port->usb2_dev (now a dangling\n   pointer to freed memory) and passes it to typec_partner_unlink_device()\n   -> sysfs_remove_link() -> dev_name() on the freed device, corrupting\n   the typec/UCSI partner state.\n\nThis corruption leaves the Thunderbolt tunnel in an inconsistent state on\nthe next dock hot-plug.  On affected hardware the dock's I225/igc NIC fails\nto enumerate: AER fires a slot reset while the igc driver is still\ninitialising (\"PCIe link lost\"), and the subsequent igc_reset attempt hits\nigc_rd32 on an already-detached device:\n\n    igc 0000:2e:00.0 eth0: PCIe link lost, device now detached\n    igc: Failed to read reg 0x0!\n    WARNING: CPU: 9 PID: 129 at drivers/net/ethernet/intel/igc/igc_main.c:7005\n             igc_rd32+0xa4/0xc0 [igc]\n    Call Trace:\n     igc_disable_pcie_master+0x16/0xa0 [igc]\n     igc_reset_hw_base+0x14/0x170 [igc]\n     igc_reset+0x63/0x110 [igc]\n     igc_io_slot_reset+0x9e/0xd0 [igc]\n     report_slot_reset+0x5d/0xc0\n     pcie_do_recovery+0x209/0x400\n     aer_isr_one_error_type+0x235/0x430\n     aer_isr+0x4e/0x80\n     irq_thread+0xf4/0x1f0\n\n4. UCSI later handles the PD partner-disconnect and calls\n   typec_unregister_partner(), which still sees the stale port->usb2_dev\n   and tries to remove its sysfs link a second time:\n\n   kernfs: can not remove 'typec', no directory\n   WARNING: CPU: 6 PID: 55 at fs/kernfs/dir.c:1706 kernfs_remove_by_name_ns+0xe9/0xf0\n   Workqueue: events ucsi_handle_connector_change [typec_ucsi]\n   Call Trace:\n    sysfs_remove_link+0x19/0x50\n    typec_unregister_partner+0x6e/0x120 [typec]\n    ucsi_unregister_partner+0x107/0x150 [typec_ucsi]\n    ucsi_handle_connector_change+0x3ec/0x490 [typec_ucsi]\n    process_one_work+0x18e/0x3e0\n    worker_thread+0x2e3/0x420\n    kthread+0x10a/0x230\n    ret_from_fork+0x121/0x140\n    ret_from_fork_asm+0x1a/0x30\n\n   With worse timing the same stale pointer is dereferenced after the\n   backing memory is freed, turning the warning into a use-after-free.\n\nFix the asymmetry: call typec_deattach() before clearing\nport_dev->connector, matching what connector_bind() does on the bind side.\ntypec_partner_deattach() is already protected by port->partner_link_lock,\nso it serialises safely with the concurrent typec_unregister_partner() path.\n\nFixes: 11110783f5ea (\"usb: Inform the USB Type-C class about enumerated devices\")\nCc: stable <stable@kernel.org>\nSigned-off-by: Chia-Lin Kao (AceLan) <acelan.kao@canonical.com>\nReviewed-by: Heikki Krogerus <heikki.krogerus@linux.intel.com>\nLink: https://patch.msgid.link/20260611071201.1235545-1-acelan.kao@canonical.com\nSigned-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>",

connector_unbind() is the mirror of connector_bind(), but it is missing
the symmetric call to typec_deattach() that connector_bind() makes via:

    if (port_dev->child)
        typec_attach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);

When a Thunderbolt dock is unplugged, two teardown paths race:

1. The component framework calls connector_unbind() first, which sets
   port_dev->connector = NULL without calling typec_deattach().  This
   leaves port->usb2_dev/port->usb3_dev in struct typec_port pointing at
   the USB device that is about to be freed.

2. usb_disconnect() then calls typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, ...),
   but port_dev->connector is already NULL, so the call is a no-op and
   port->usb2_dev is never cleared.

3. Concurrently, UCSI detects a PD partner-disconnect event and calls
   typec_unregister_partner(), which reads port->usb2_dev (now a dangling
   pointer to freed memory) and passes it to typec_partner_unlink_device()
   -> sysfs_remove_link() -> dev_name() on the freed device, corrupting
   the typec/UCSI partner state.

This corruption leaves the Thunderbolt tunnel in an inconsistent state on
the next dock hot-plug.  On affected hardware the dock's I225/igc NIC fails
to enumerate: AER fires a slot reset while the igc driver is still
initialising ("PCIe link lost"), and the subsequent igc_reset attempt hits
igc_rd32 on an already-detached device:

## Root cause

This is a Type-C/USB teardown race, not a kernfs defect.

The relevant tree is Linux `v7.0` (`028ef9c96e`, as checked out in `/workspace/linux`). The bug is present there.

### 1. UCSI receives the disconnect and unregisters the partner

`drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c`:

- `ucsi_handle_connector_change()` handles `UCSI_CONSTAT_CONNECT_CHANGE` at lines **1306–1326**.
- For a disconnected connector it calls:

```c
ucsi_unregister_partner(con);
```

at line **1325**.

- `ucsi_unregister_partner()` then calls:

```c
typec_unregister_partner(con->partner);
```

at line **1151**.

Thus the reported path is:

```text
ucsi_handle_connector_change()
  -> ucsi_unregister_partner()
     -> typec_unregister_partner()
```

`ucsi_connector_change()` schedules the work at `ucsi.c:1371–1382`, explaining the `events` workqueue context.

### 2. `typec_unregister_partner()` removes links for remembered USB devices

`drivers/usb/typec/class.c`:

```c
static void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner,
                                        struct device *dev)
{
        sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));
        sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
        ...
}
```

This is at lines **906–913**.

The `"typec"` link is initially created by `typec_partner_link_device()`:

```c
ret = sysfs_create_link(&dev->kobj, &partner->dev.kobj, "typec");
```

at `class.c:888–904`.

During partner removal, `typec_unregister_partner()` uses the cached USB-device pointers in `struct typec_port`:

```c
if (port->usb2_dev) {
        typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb2_dev);
        port->usb2_dev = NULL;
}
if (port->usb3_dev) {
        typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb3_dev);
        port->usb3_dev = NULL;
}
```

at `class.c:1183–1191`.

The warning therefore comes specifically through:

```text
typec_unregister_partner()
  -> typec_partner_unlink_device()
     -> sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")
        -> kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()
```

The offending Type-C function is **`typec_partner_unlink_device()`**, called from **`typec_unregister_partner()`**.

## Why the kernfs removal returns `-ENOENT`

`fs/kernfs/dir.c:1715–1733` documents and implements the warning:

```c
if (!parent) {
        WARN(1, KERN_WARNING
             "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n", name);
        return -ENOENT;
}
```

`sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")` eventually calls this with the kernfs node associated with `dev->kobj` as the parent.

The underlying problem is that `port->usb2_dev` or `port->usb3_dev` can be stale:

1. `typec_partner_link_device()` stores the USB device indirectly in the Type-C port state through the attach path. The corresponding Type-C attach/deattach handling is in `drivers/usb/typec/class.c`.

2. USB component binding calls Type-C attach when a USB child already exists:

   `drivers/usb/core/port.c:695–719`, especially:

   ```c
   if (port_dev->child)
           typec_attach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);
   ```

3. However, the current `connector_unbind()` implementation only removes the component links and clears the connector pointer:

   `drivers/usb/core/port.c:722–729`:

   ```c
   sysfs_remove_link(&connector->kobj, dev_name(dev));
   sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");
   port_dev->connector = NULL;
   ```

   It does **not** call `typec_deattach()` first.

4. Later USB teardown can therefore run with `port_dev->connector == NULL`; the normal Type-C deattach operation becomes a no-op. The Type-C port retains `usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` pointing at a USB device whose kobject and sysfs directory are subsequently removed.

5. UCSI independently processes the partner-disconnect event. At `ucsi.c:1324–1325`, it calls `ucsi_unregister_partner()`, which reaches `typec_unregister_partner()`.

6. `typec_unregister_partner()` still sees the stale USB-device pointer at `class.c:1184–1190` and calls `typec_partner_unlink_device()`. Its second removal:

   ```c
   sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
   ```

   at `class.c:909,`

   attempts to remove a link below a kobject whose kernfs directory has already gone away. Kernfs consequently sees a missing parent and emits:

```text
kernfs: can not remove 'typec', no directory
```

and returns `-ENOENT`.

With worse timing, the stale pointer can also become a use-after-free rather than merely producing this warning.

## Is the fix already in this tree?

No.

The checked-out tree contains the asymmetric code:

- `drivers/usb/core/port.c:716–717` calls `typec_attach()` during bind.
- `drivers/usb/core/port.c:722–729` does not call `typec_deattach()` during unbind.

There is no corresponding fix in the local `v7.0` history or source.

## Upstream fix

An upstream fix exists:

**Commit:** `e0b291fe117964037e0ba382eff4bb365d531c3a`  
**Subject:** `usb: core: port: Deattach Type-C connector on component unbind`

The patch modifies `drivers/usb/core/port.c`, adding to `connector_unbind()` before clearing `port_dev->connector`:

```c
if (port_dev->child)
        typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);
```

The resulting ordering is:

```c
sysfs_remove_link(&connector->kobj, dev_name(dev));
sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");
if (port_dev->child)
        typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);
port_dev->connector = NULL;
```

This is the required symmetry with `connector_bind()` and ensures that Type-C clears its USB-device association before the USB kobject is destroyed. The commit is marked for stable backporting and cites:

```text
Fixes: 11110783f5ea
("usb: Inform the USB Type-C class about enumerated devices")
Cc: stable@kernel.org
```

So the practical fix is not in `drivers/usb/typec` or `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi`; it is in **`drivers/usb/core/port.c`**, fixing the missing Type-C deattach during USB component unbind.

15:    "message": "usb: core: port: Deattach Type-C connector on component unbind

connector_unbind() is the mirror of connector_bind(), but it is missing
the symmetric call to typec_deattach() that connector_bind() makes via:

    if (port_dev->child)
        typec_attach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);

When a Thunderbolt dock is unplugged, two teardown paths race:

1. The component framework calls connector_unbind() first, which sets
   port_dev->connector = NULL without calling typec_deattach().  This
   leaves port->usb2_dev/port->usb3_dev in struct typec_port pointing at
   the USB device that is about to be freed.

2. usb_disconnect() then calls typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, ...),
   but port_dev->connector is already NULL, so the call is a no-op and
   port->usb2_dev is never cleared.

3. Concurrently, UCSI detects a PD partner-disconnect event and calls
   typec_unregister_partner(), which reads port->usb2_dev (now a dangling
   pointer to freed memory) and passes it to typec_partner_unlink_device()
   -> sysfs_remove_link() -> dev_name() on the freed device, corrupting
   the typec/UCSI partner state.

This corruption leaves the Thunderbolt tunnel in an inconsistent state on
the next dock hot-plug.  On affected hardware the dock's I225/igc NIC fails
to enumerate: AER fires a slot reset while the igc driver is still
initialising ("PCIe link lost"), and the subsequent igc_reset attempt hits
igc_rd32 on an already-detached device:

    igc 0000:2e:00.0 eth0: PCIe link lost, device now detached
    igc: Failed to read reg 0x0!
    WARNING: CPU: 9 PID: 129 at drivers/net/ethernet/intel/igc/igc_main.c:7005
             igc_rd32+0xa4/0xc0 [igc]
    Call Trace:
     igc_disable_pcie_master+0x16/0xa0 [igc]
     igc_reset_hw_base+0x14/0x170 [igc]
     igc_reset+0x63/0x110 [igc]
     igc_io_slot_reset+0x9e/0xd0 [igc]
     report_slot_reset+0x5d/0xc0
     pcie_do_recovery+0x209/0x400
     aer_isr_one_error_type+0x235/0x430
     aer_isr+0x4e/0x80
     irq_thread+0xf4/0x1f0

4. UCSI later handles the PD partner-disconnect and calls
   typec_unregister_partner(), which still sees the stale port->usb2_dev
   and tries to remove its sysfs link a second time:

   kernfs: can not remove 'typec', no directory
   WARNING: CPU: 6 PID: 55 at fs/kernfs/dir.c:1706 kernfs_remove_by_name_ns+0xe9/0xf0
   Workqueue: events ucsi_handle_connector_change [typec_ucsi]
   Call Trace:
    sysfs_remove_link+0x19/0x50
    typec_unregister_partner+0x6e/0x120 [typec]
    ucsi_unregister_partner+0x107/0x150 [typec_ucsi]
    ucsi_handle_connector_change+0x3ec/0x490 [typec_ucsi]
    process_one_work+0x18e/0x3e0
    worker_thread+0x2e3/0x420
    kthread+0x10a/0x230
    ret_from_fork+0x121/0x140
    ret_from_fork_asm+0x1a/0x30

   With worse timing the same stale pointer is dereferenced after the
   backing memory is freed, turning the warning into a use-after-free.

Fix the asymmetry: call typec_deattach() before clearing
port_dev->connector, matching what connector_bind() does on the bind side.
typec_partner_deattach() is already protected by port->partner_link_lock,
so it serialises safely with the concurrent typec_unregister_partner() path.

content.text:
## Root cause

This is a Type-C/USB teardown race, not a kernfs defect.

The relevant tree is Linux `v7.0` (`028ef9c96e`, as checked out in `/workspace/linux`). The bug is present there.

### 1. UCSI receives the disconnect and unregisters the partner

`drivers/usb/typec/ucsi/ucsi.c`:

- `ucsi_handle_connector_change()` handles `UCSI_CONSTAT_CONNECT_CHANGE` at lines **1306–1326**.
- For a disconnected connector it calls:

```c
ucsi_unregister_partner(con);
```

at line **1325**.

- `ucsi_unregister_partner()` then calls:

```c
typec_unregister_partner(con->partner);
```

at line **1151**.

Thus the reported path is:

```text
ucsi_handle_connector_change()
  -> ucsi_unregister_partner()
     -> typec_unregister_partner()
```

`ucsi_connector_change()` schedules the work at `ucsi.c:1371–1382`, explaining the `events` workqueue context.

### 2. `typec_unregister_partner()` removes links for remembered USB devices

`drivers/usb/typec/class.c`:

```c
static void typec_partner_unlink_device(struct typec_partner *partner,
                                        struct device *dev)
{
        sysfs_remove_link(&partner->dev.kobj, dev_name(dev));
        sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
        ...
}
```

This is at lines **906–913**.

The `"typec"` link is initially created by `typec_partner_link_device()`:

```c
ret = sysfs_create_link(&dev->kobj, &partner->dev.kobj, "typec");
```

at `class.c:888–904`.

During partner removal, `typec_unregister_partner()` uses the cached USB-device pointers in `struct typec_port`:

```c
if (port->usb2_dev) {
        typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb2_dev);
        port->usb2_dev = NULL;
}
if (port->usb3_dev) {
        typec_partner_unlink_device(partner, port->usb3_dev);
        port->usb3_dev = NULL;
}
```

at `class.c:1183–1191`.

The warning therefore comes specifically through:

```text
typec_unregister_partner()
  -> typec_partner_unlink_device()
     -> sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")
        -> kernfs_remove_by_name_ns()
```

The offending Type-C function is **`typec_partner_unlink_device()`**, called from **`typec_unregister_partner()`**.

## Why the kernfs removal returns `-ENOENT`

`fs/kernfs/dir.c:1715–1733` documents and implements the warning:

```c
if (!parent) {
        WARN(1, KERN_WARNING
             "kernfs: can not remove '%s', no directory\n", name);
        return -ENOENT;
}
```

`sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec")` eventually calls this with the kernfs node associated with `dev->kobj` as the parent.

The underlying problem is that `port->usb2_dev` or `port->usb3_dev` can be stale:

1. `typec_partner_link_device()` stores the USB device indirectly in the Type-C port state through the attach path. The corresponding Type-C attach/deattach handling is in `drivers/usb/typec/class.c`.

2. USB component binding calls Type-C attach when a USB child already exists:

   `drivers/usb/core/port.c:695–719`, especially:

   ```c
   if (port_dev->child)
           typec_attach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);
   ```

3. However, the current `connector_unbind()` implementation only removes the component links and clears the connector pointer:

   `drivers/usb/core/port.c:722–729`:

   ```c
   sysfs_remove_link(&connector->kobj, dev_name(dev));
   sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");
   port_dev->connector = NULL;
   ```

   It does **not** call `typec_deattach()` first.

4. Later USB teardown can therefore run with `port_dev->connector == NULL`; the normal Type-C deattach operation becomes a no-op. The Type-C port retains `usb2_dev`/`usb3_dev` pointing at a USB device whose kobject and sysfs directory are subsequently removed.

5. UCSI independently processes the partner-disconnect event. At `ucsi.c:1324–1325`, it calls `ucsi_unregister_partner()`, which reaches `typec_unregister_partner()`.

6. `typec_unregister_partner()` still sees the stale USB-device pointer at `class.c:1184–1190` and calls `typec_partner_unlink_device()`. Its second removal:

   ```c
   sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "typec");
   ```

   at `class.c:909,`

   attempts to remove a link below a kobject whose kernfs directory has already gone away. Kernfs consequently sees a missing parent and emits:

```text
kernfs: can not remove 'typec', no directory
```

and returns `-ENOENT`.

With worse timing, the stale pointer can also become a use-after-free rather than merely producing this warning.

## Is the fix already in this tree?

No.

The checked-out tree contains the asymmetric code:

- `drivers/usb/core/port.c:716–717` calls `typec_attach()` during bind.
- `drivers/usb/core/port.c:722–729` does not call `typec_deattach()` during unbind.

There is no corresponding fix in the local `v7.0` history or source.

## Upstream fix

An upstream fix exists:

**Commit:** `e0b291fe117964037e0ba382eff4bb365d531c3a`  
**Subject:** `usb: core: port: Deattach Type-C connector on component unbind`

The patch modifies `drivers/usb/core/port.c`, adding to `connector_unbind()` before clearing `port_dev->connector`:

```c
if (port_dev->child)
        typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);
```

The resulting ordering is:

```c
sysfs_remove_link(&connector->kobj, dev_name(dev));
sysfs_remove_link(&dev->kobj, "connector");
if (port_dev->child)
        typec_deattach(port_dev->connector, &port_dev->child->dev);
port_dev->connector = NULL;
```

This is the required symmetry with `connector_bind()` and ensures that Type-C clears its USB-device association before the USB kobject is destroyed. The commit is marked for stable backporting and cites:

```text
Fixes: 11110783f5ea
("usb: Inform the USB Type-C class about enumerated devices")
Cc: stable@kernel.org
```

So the practical fix is not in `drivers/usb/typec` or `drivers/usb/typec/ucsi`; it is in **`drivers/usb/core/port.c`**, fixing the missing Type-C deattach during USB component unbind.
